html:
Muhammad Ali was an Albanian-born Ottoman officer who made himself master of Egypt, ruling it from 1805 to 1848. He is often called the founder of modern Egypt.

He arrived with Ottoman troops sent to retake Egypt after Napoleon's invasion. In the chaos he won over the people of Cairo, had the sultan name him governor, and in 1811 had the Mamluk beys massacred at the Citadel.

  • He built a conscript army and navy on European lines and sent students to France.
  • He set up state factories and monopolies, and made long-staple cotton the country's export.
  • His armies took Sudan, the Hejaz, and for a time Syria, and twice threatened the Ottoman sultan himself.

The European powers forced him back in 1840, but let his family keep Egypt as a hereditary governorship. His descendants ruled until the 1952 revolution led by Nasser.
sum: Muhammad Ali was an Albanian-born Ottoman officer who made himself master of Egypt, ruling it from 1805 to 1848. He is often called the founder of modern Egypt.
